theme_central: "The Bride of the Qur'an": a rhythmic hymn of Ar-Rahman's blessings, punctuated by the refrain repeated 31 times — "Then which of your Lord's blessings will you deny?"
sources_note: 3-unit structure precisely sourced (medium.com/@soltlane, Wikipedia Ar-Rahman): 1-30, 31-45, 46-78. Refrain confirmed repeated 31 times.

branches.title: Ar-Rahman taught the Qur'an
branches.resume: He taught the Qur'an, created man, taught him clear expression.

children.t: Ar-Rahman teaches the Qur'an, creates man, teaches him clear expression

branches.title: Signs of creation, balance
branches.resume: Sun and moon by precise calculation, the fair balance, man from clay and jinn from fire.

children.t: Sun and moon precisely set, stars and trees prostrating, the fair balance
Creation of man from ringing clay and jinn from pure fire

branches.title: The two seas, all perishes but Allah
branches.resume: The two seas that meet without mixing; everything perishes except the Face of your Lord.

children.t: The two seas meeting without mixing, pearls and coral
Everything perishes except Allah's Face; every day He is upon some task

branches.title: Summons to men and jinn
branches.resume: Challenge issued to men and jinn to cross the regions of the heavens without authority.

children.t: Summons to men and jinn, cosmic challenge to cross the heavens

branches.title: Scene of the Judgment
branches.resume: The sky split open, flames and smoke, criminals recognized by their marks, seized and cast into Hell.

children.t: The sky split open, criminals recognized by their marks, seized for Hell

branches.title: The gardens of Paradise
branches.resume: For whoever fears standing before his Lord: two gardens, then two more — springs, fruits, houris, closing on Allah's munificence.

children.t: First two gardens: gushing springs, fruits in pairs, chaste houris
Two additional gardens; closing on Allah's greatness and munificence
